immediate.judge: I will rule on the issues as currently organised. We move to the verdict stage.

conditional.judge: I will start by proposing a conditional mediation that separates the core responsibilities. The will-drafting procedure, the difference between the notarised copy and the handwritten draft, and the long-running care and account flow will not be bundled into one matter.

dialogues.speaker: a
dialogues.text: Yoon Tae-seong's side can hear a conditional mediation. But by what procedure the will was drawn up has to be put on paper first, or the same confusion just keeps coming back.

dialogues.speaker: b
dialogues.text: Yoon Jung-hoo's side can hear the conditional terms as well. But the difference between the notarised copy and the handwritten draft, and the situation in which I was at our mother's side, must be addressed together.

postpone.judge: I will fix only the facts that can be confirmed today and reserve the rest. How each side understood our mother's wishes will be looked at separately, between record and testimony.

dialogues.speaker: a
dialogues.text: Yoon Tae-seong's side can accept reserving a decision. But the will-drafting procedure and our mother's capacity to decide at least have to be drawn out today, or further confusion will only grow.

dialogues.speaker: b
dialogues.text: Yoon Jung-hoo's side also believes the circumstances need a closer look before any hasty conclusion. But please make it clear that reserving a decision is not the same as being cleared.

fact_first.judge: Before any solution, I will fix the facts. The will-drafting procedure, the difference between the handwritten draft and the notarised copy, and the order of the long-running care and account flow come first.

dialogues.speaker: a
dialogues.text: Yoon Tae-seong's side agrees with sorting facts out first. At minimum, the will-drafting procedure and the question of our mother's capacity have to be fixed against the records first.

dialogues.speaker: b
dialogues.text: Yoon Jung-hoo's side can accept facts before solutions. But the situation in which I was at our mother's side, and the responsibility for the paperwork, have to be looked at separately from emotion.
